A lovely dream—until he fades from view. But where do I find them, where, those earthly wings, companions to the wings of the spirit? Yet everywhere, in each of us, we harbor the desire to rise above, to surge, to soar along, when high in the blue immensity of heaven the lark pipes its trilling song; when high above pine-clad crags the eagle hovers on wings wide spread; when at evening the crane flaps slowly homeward over sleepy ponds and marches.

@@U00267@@
Yes, well, I’ve had my aberrant moments, too, but I must confess P’ve never felt such an urge. You see one field and forest you've seen them all, and soon enough, too. And as for envying a bird its flight, no no, not me, glad to say. How differently the spirit’s pleasures bear us from book to book, from page to page! How bright and beautiful winter nights are then, every limb snug and warm. Ah, and then you unroll an ancient parchment and heaven spreads out before you!

@@U00269@@
Yes, and this is the force that drives you. You know only the one urge, never strive to know the other! Ach! Two souls cohabit in my breast, each one struggling to tear itself from the other! The one, like a coarse lover,

@@U00265@@
一个美丽的梦——直到他从视野中消失。但我在哪里可以找到它们，在哪里，那些尘世的翅膀，精神之翼的伴侣？然而，在我们每个人的每一处地方，当云雀在蔚蓝无际的天空中高高地奏出颤抖的歌声时，我们都怀有一种飞升、澎湃、翱翔的渴望；当雄鹰在松树覆盖的峭壁上空张开翅膀盘旋时；到了晚上，鹤在沉睡的池塘和行军上空缓慢地拍打着翅膀回家。

@@U00267@@
是的，我也有过异常的时刻，但我必须承认，我从未有过这样的冲动。你看到了一片田野和一片森林，你也很快就看到了它们。至于羡慕鸟儿的飞行，不，不，不是我，很高兴地说。每本书、每一页所带给我们的精神愉悦是多么不同啊！那时的冬夜是多么明亮美丽，四肢舒适温暖。啊，然后你展开一张古老的羊皮纸，天堂就展现在你面前！

@@U00269@@
